reference_rule: Evaluate Opus5.5 and Astra on identical frozen questions and accepted variants. Report both references, all-request and completed scores, refusals, truncations, and worst/best missing-response bounds. Strongest tested reference is the largest point accuracy; report whether completion handling changes the ordering. No cap or model change after seeing final answers without a separately identified sensitivity study.
target_interpretation: 79–81% is a point-accuracy target for the stronger reference, not a demand that a95% interval fit wholly inside the2pp band. Require all-request and completed estimates plus missing-response bounds in band so missing answers do not create apparent target attainment. Report95% intervals visibly. Precision below1pp must be checked for both references, not inferred from Opus alone.
uncertainty_analysis: Both iid and exact-family cluster sandwich SE must be below.01 for both references. Report all-request and completed ratio SE, include zero-completion family contributions, whole-family bootstrap95% intervals and class-stratified bootstrap sensitivity with fixed seeds. Sparse-class counts and exact-family versus etymological-dependence limits remain explicit. Do not treat repeated aorists as independent.
fixed_extension_rule: All chosenN questions are primary evaluation, including every committed extension. Run to thatN irrespective of interim accuracy or precision. If budget or transport failure stops earlier, report incomplete evaluation and all available counts without claiming the frozen precision target.
precision_failure_rule: If either model has either iidSE>=.01 or clusterSE>=.01 at committedN, explicitly report precision unmet. Do not add questions based on SE or accuracy; a new preregistered evaluation cannot retroactively qualify this one.
validity_rule: Uniform source-driven scope predicates may quarantine original inputs across all outcomes. Preserve original membership/scores, publish exact changed-scope denominators and reasons, and do not fill holes based on model errors. If changing scope materially changes weights or precision, the predeclared primary target is not silently repaired.
